title: Send the gradient back through batch norm and layer norm
brief: Compute the gradients of the scale and shift, then the compact formula for the input gradient, and check both layers against finite differences and two sanity properties.
hints: affine_param_grads sums over axis 0 for both layers: dbeta = dout.sum(axis=0) and dgamma = (dout * xhat).sum(axis=0). gamma and beta have one entry per feature and are shared by every example.
The input gradient is dx = (istd / M) * (M * dxhat - dxhat.sum(axis, keepdims=True) - xhat * (dxhat * xhat).sum(axis, keepdims=True)), with dxhat = dout * gamma and M = dout.shape[axis].
The cache is (xhat, istd, gamma, axis). Batch norm and layer norm differ only in the axis stored in it, so one helper can serve both backward functions.
Check your dx against a finite difference of the scalar np.sum(dout * forward(x)[0]). If the check fails by a small amount everywhere, look at the sign of the variance term.
